01.r: Links this scene to the teaching before it.

02.r: Jesus sits down facing the treasury.
02.n: An aorist participle, literally 'having sat down'. Abbott-Smith's intransitive sense is 'to sit down, be seated, sit'. Our text does not name Jesus here; see the note on the Textus Receptus.

05.r: Where he sits: facing the treasury.
05.n: Abbott-Smith gives 'over against, opposite, before', and lists this verse among its uses as a preposition.

07.r: The place in the temple where offerings were received.
07.n: Abbott-Smith builds it from γάζα, treasure, and φυλακή, guard, and notes the Septuagint's use of it for a temple treasury. He adds that it apparently also names the trumpet-shaped chests used for the gifts, which fits watching people put money in.

08.r: He watches the givers for some time.
08.n: An imperfect: ongoing watching, not a glance. Abbott-Smith derives it from θεωρός, a spectator, and gives 'to look at, gaze, behold'.

09.r: He watches the manner of the giving, not only the fact.

10.r: The crowd present in the temple.

11.n: Abbott-Smith: 'a moving crowd or multitude of persons, a throng'.

12.r: People put their coins into the chests.
12.n: Abbott-Smith's sense is 'to throw, cast, put, place', first used of a missile. A present tense kept inside the report of what he watched.

13.r: Copper coins, the common small money of the crowd.
13.n: Abbott-Smith's sense is 'copper', and by extension 'copper coin', with this verse listed. Five translations make it 'money'; the YLT keeps the metal as 'brass'.

17.r: Adds the rich to the general crowd.

18.r: Not a few of the rich.

19.n: An adjective used as a noun, 'rich ones'. Abbott-Smith: 'rich, wealthy'.

20.r: The rich go on giving large sums.
20.n: An imperfect: a continuing scene. The same verb as 'puts' earlier in the verse.

tr_note: The Textus Receptus names the subject, ὁ Ἰησοῦς, 'Jesus', after 'having sat down'. That is the KJV's 'And Jesus sat'; our text leaves the subject unstated, and the ASV reads 'he sat down'.
